description: Signature evidence. Signatures are demoted, never deleted, so these patterns only need to be good enough to collapse a trailing block. The RFC 3676 delimiter is the only high confidence rule; everything else is positional evidence that the sequence classifier weighs.

phrases.pattern: ^\s*(Von meinem|Envoy. de mon|Enviado desde mi|Inviato da|Verzonden vanaf mijn|Skickat från min|Lähetetty|Saadetud minu|Отправлено с) .{0,60}$

^\s*(Best regards|Kind regards|Warm regards|Warmest regards|With (kind|best|warm) regards|Best wishes|All the best|Take care|Regards|Cheers|Thanks|Many thanks|Thanks (again|in advance)|Thank you|Sincerely|Best|Yours( sincerely| truly)?|Br|Rgds|Mit freundlichen Grüßen|Viele Grüße|Beste Grüße|Cordialement|Bien à vous|Saludos|Atentamente|Cordiali saluti|Groeten|Met vriendelijke groet|Med vänliga hälsningar|Vänliga hälsningar|Med venlig hilsen|Venlig hilsen|Med vennlig hilsen|Vennlig hilsen|Mvh|S pozdravem|Ystävällisin terveisin|Terveisin|Parimat|Parimate soovidega|Heade soovidega|Lugupidamisega|Tervitades|Tervitused|Terv|Kõike head|Ilusat päeva|Head aega|Austusega|Aitäh|Tänan|Tänud|Ette tänades|С уважением|Z poważaniem|Pozdrawiam)\s*[,.!;]?\s*[-\u2013\u2014]?\s*$
phrases.comment: Closing greeting. Mined from blocks the reference labelled SIGNATURE that this baseline missed, which is why the Estonian forms are here: the working corpus is roughly ten percent Estonian and those accounted for the largest group of misses. The greeting must still be the whole line; only a trailing comma, period or dash is tolerated, because 'Thanks, that works.' is prose, not a sign-off.
Labelled phone, email or web line. The email and web alternatives need their own value shape: an address or URL never starts with a digit, so folding them into the phone branch made them unmatchable.
Continental European corporate footers carry a registered office and company number. These lines are boilerplate, never authored prose.
A street line in a trailing block. Weak on its own, but it pairs with a name or a closing greeting to identify a corporate signature.
A postal code followed by a capitalised city name. Deliberately case sensitive: under the i flag the capital letter class matched any word, so a line like '12345 units shipped' counted as an address.
